text:
Ottawa arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 5-1 win in San Jose that followed an overtime loss in Los Angeles. The Senators are 2-2-1 in their last five and are playing without William Eklund, with Tim Stützle now skating beside Cozens and Zetterlund. Anaheim has had two days off but is 1-3-1 in its last five, coming off a 7-6 loss to Buffalo in which the Sabres came back from two goals down. The Ducks are missing Ryan Poehling, and Roger McQueen has taken his spot.

The chance numbers lean Ottawa's way. At five on five, the Senators have taken 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, and the Ducks 44%. Anaheim gives up 3.57 expected goals per 60 minutes, and its penalty kill sits 27th in chances allowed. Ottawa's power play is fifth in chances, so the Ducks' penalty habits matter. Ottawa's projected goalie, Jonas Johansson, has been rough: minus 0.51 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots should have produced) in three games this season, and minus 10.72 in 25 last year. We have no projected goalie for Anaheim.

Drake Batherson is on a seven-game point streak, and Stützle is at 78% for a point. For Anaheim, Cutter Gauthier is our top goal pick at 38%. Among our under-the-radar picks, Stephen Halliday of Ottawa plays about 11 minutes a night but has 2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games, and Mikael Granlund of Anaheim has more ice time than usual and a line that creates chances.
